newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Airways cargo workers on strike.
newsitem.headline: Thai Airways cargo workers on strike.

text.p: Cargo handling workers of Thai Airways International Plc started a strike at Bangkok's Don Muang airport on Monday to press their demand for the government to overturn its decision to launch a new Thai cargo airline.
A spokesman of the Thai Airways Employees Association said over 1,000 off-duty staff of the airline's cargo section staged a rally at the airport for six hours in the morning.
He said the workers planned to hold a similar protest at the prime minister's office at Government House on Tuesday.

Airline industry sources said up to 70 percent of the airport's cargo services, especially those for outbound freight, were affected by the strike which took place during a coincidental breakdown of the airport's telephone systems.

"All outbound freight of several airlines that are normally handled by Thai Airways ground workers are affected since noon as they could not be moved out of locked warehouses," a source at an air freight company said.
He said no flights were cancelled because of the strike but many planes left with little or no cargoes.
The Thai cabinet on October 15 approved a communications ministry proposal for Thai Airways to hold a 40 percent stake in Thai Air Cargo Co Ltd.

"The new airline decision greatly depresses our morale. We will continue to press our demand until either the government changes its decision or provides an assurance that the new cargo airline will not affect our benefits and welfare," the employees association spokesman said.
